simple.meaning: מַשְׁרוֹקִי (mashrôwqîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “a (musical) pipe (from its whistling sound).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַשְׁרוֹקִי (H4953) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 3:5, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַשְׁרוֹקִי (H4953) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַשְׁרוֹקִי (H4953) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַשְׁרוֹקִי (mashrôwqîy) / H4953 is traced through Daniel 3:5, Daniel 3:7, Daniel 3:10, Daniel 3:15 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H4953. mashroqi [ מַשְׁרוֺקִי ] noun feminine pipe (compare Syriac (rare)); — emphatic מַשְׁרוֺקִיתָא Dan 3:5 , 7 , 15 , ׳מַשְׁרֹק 3:10 .

occurrences.englishText: that whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, you fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king has set up.

Therefore at that time, when all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, all the peoples, the nations, and the languages, fell down and worshiped the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.
You, O king, have made a decree, that every man that hears the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, shall fall down and worship the golden image;

Now if you are ready whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music to fall down and worship the image which I have made, good; but if you don’t worship, you shall be cast the same hour into the middle of a burning fiery furnace. Who is that god that will deliver you out of my hands?”
